summary.pack_description:
Collect some of the greatest moments of the 2022-23 Stanley Cup Playoffs, culminating with the Vegas Golden Knights first championship in franchise history over the improbable second wild card run of the Florida Panthers.

The Hunt for Stanley 2023 Debut LE Pack features series-clinching goals, improbable saves, and more from Adin Hill, Matthew Tkachuk, John Tavares, Wyatt Johnston, Oliver Bjorkstrand, Dougie Hamilton and other playoff heroes!

Each pack contains 1 The Hunt for Stanley 2023 highlight, 3 Base highlights, plus 1 mystery highlight that could be from Making the Mark, The Hunt for Stanley 2023, Opening Ice, or Base sets.

release.name: The Hunt for Stanley 2023 Debut LE Pack
release.description:
Sale Starts: Friday, Aug 25 at 1PM ET / 10AM PT

Eligibility: Beta users only. Not a beta user? Click here to create your account.

 

Price: $35 USD

# Packs Available: 2500 packs total. 1000 will be available at the start of the drop, with additional inventory released at 5pm and 9pm ET to accommodate fans in worldwide time zones. Sales will end after 24 hours, with remaining packs being distributed later during Series 1.

 

Purchase Limit: Six (6) pack limit per person. Once the “Buy Now” process has started, users will have 10 minutes to complete checkout before the pack(s) is released for another collector to purchase.

 

Highlights Per Pack: 5

Pack Contents (Highlight Rarity, Edition Size):

  • One (1) The Hunt for Stanley 2023 highlight (Limited #/500)
  • Three (3) Base highlights (Core #/1500) – selected randomly from both the original and expansion sets
  • One (1) highlight with the following probabilities:
    • 46% Base highlight (Core) from the 2022-23 Expansion set
    • 31% The Hunt for Stanley 2023 highlight (Limited)
    • 20% Opening Ice highlight (Rare)
    • 3% Making the Mark highlight (Epic) – includes new career and season-defining highlights from Linus Ullmark, Erik Karlsson, and Steven Stamkos

 

Payment Methods Accepted: Most major credit and debit cards. Payments will be made via registered payment processor MoonPay; except when not available, payments will be processed via Stripe. Cryptocurrency purchases and ACH transfers into your NHL Breakaway account which can be used for purchases coming later in 2023.

 

Fan Marketplace: Packs and highlights will be eligible to be sold to other collectors on the NHL Breakaway fan marketplace later in 2023.

 

Transferability: Packs and highlights will be eligible to be gifted to other NHL Breakaway users later in 2023.

 

Blockchain: Polygon

 

Sets Included:

  • Full Highlights List
  • The Hunt for Stanley 2023, Series 1 - Preview
  • Opening Ice, Series 1 - Preview
  • Base, Series 1 - Preview (Expansion) | Preview (Original)
  • Making the Mark, Series 1 - Preview

 

Collection Guarantee: Series 1 highlights will only be distributed during Series 1, which ends ~September 2024. We will not issue more than the edition limit we have set. Any editions not distributed in packs will not be distributed after the series end date (See FAQ for “Uncirculated Editions”)

 

All sales subject to Terms

summary.name: The Hunt for Stanley 2023
summary.description: The Stanley Cup Playoffs are the most grueling and intense postseason in all of sports, and they are a true test of a team's skill, endurance, and mental toughness. The excitement of the playoffs is palpable, with every game feeling like a do-or-die battle for survival. The physicality of the games is ramped up, and every player knows that they have to bring their A-game if they want to advance to the next round. The grind of the playoffs is intense, with teams playing every other night for weeks on end. Injuries can pile up, and exhaustion can set in, but the desire to win the ultimate prize keeps players pushing themselves to their limits. It's a thrilling and exhausting experience that only the best teams are able to survive and emerge victorious.

summary.name: David Pastrnak
summary.description:
An electrifying and dynamic player, David Pastrnak dances around the Seattle Kraken defenseman and goes top cheese for one of his career-high 61 goals in 2022-23. Pastrnak broke into the NHL as an 18-year-old in 2014-15 and scored 301 goals through his first eight seasons – the most among all Bruins players in that span. The Czech-born winger won the Maurice “Rocket” Richard Trophy in 2019-20 alongside Alex Ovechkin as they tied for the most goals in the League that season (48 in 70 GP).

summary.name: Tage Thompson
summary.description:
Tage Thompson was a highlight machine during the 2022-23 season. Here he scores his third goal of the game to secure a hat trick and a six-point night in an 8-3 victory for the Buffalo Sabres. The 6' 6" forward stops on a dime after receiving the pass in the slot and then makes a beautiful backhand-to-forehand move for the goal, which causes teammate Rasmus Dahlin to grab his head in awe.

summary.name: Nathan MacKinnon
summary.description:
Nathan MacKinnon turns on the afterburners wheeling the puck up-ice, splits the Edmonton Oilers defense and makes a nice backhand-to-forehand move before beating the goaltender to give the Colorado Avalanche their first goal of the game. A player with elite speed and immense talent, his third-period tally got the Avalanche back in the game in a contest they ultimately won in overtime.

summary.name: Jason Robertson
summary.description:
An emerging star, Jason Robertson shows his poise and vision with the puck in netting his third goal of the night for the hat trick in front of the Dallas crowd. After drawing in the Anaheim Ducks defenders, he works a give-and-go with Miro Heiskanen to create space. After getting the puck back, he puts a seeing-eye shot to the far side past the netminder. Robertson led the Dallas Stars with 46 goals in 2022-23, the most by any Stars player since 1993-94 when Mike Modano scored 50 goals during the club’s first season in Texas after relocating from Minnesota. Robertson finished 2022-23 with 109 points as he became the first Stars player with 100+ points in a season since the club began play in Dallas.

summary.name: Leon Draisaitl
summary.description:
A dual-threat superstar that can set up others as much as he can finish plays himself, Leon Draisaitl scores a beauty goal here. After a give-and-go at the blueline, Draisaitl walks the defender with a nice move and then finishes with a backhand snipe. The Edmonton Oilers forward collected 744 points over his first nine NHL seasons from 2014-15 to 2022-23, trailing only teammate Connor McDavid (850 points) for the most points among all NHL players in that span. Draisaitl won the Hart Memorial Trophy, Art Ross Trophy and Ted Lindsay Award in 2019-20.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Matthew Tkachuk
summary.description:
Coming off a career-high 104-point season with the Calgary Flames in 2021-22, Matthew Tkachuk improved upon those totals by collecting 109 points in his first campaign with the Florida Panthers – including this highlight-reel goal on Dec. 8, 2022. Skating down the right side and realizing the Detroit Red Wings defender is shutting down the pass, Tkachuk makes a backhand-to-forehand move to protect the puck before he roofs it top shelf on the far side.

summary.name: Cale Makar
summary.description:
Dynamic Colorado Avalanche defenseman Cale Makar makes a nice read on the play by picking off the pass and breaking up-ice with speed before pulling up and firing a wrister far side for the unassisted tally. The smooth-skating Makar has had an incredible start to his young career having won a Stanley Cup, Conn Smythe Trophy, James Norris Memorial Trophy and Calder Memorial Trophy within his first three seasons in the League.

summary.name: Connor McDavid
summary.description:
An absolutely thrilling scoring machine, Connor McDavid displays his world-class acceleration and finishing abilities. In overtime, McDavid curls for the pass before turning on the jets to blow by the defenders and roofs the puck top shelf in-tight at top speed for the game-winning goal. McDavid collected 850 points in his first eight NHL seasons (in only 569 games) – by far the most by any player since he entered the League in 2015-16. McDavid had 64 goals and 153 points in 2022-23 to win his first career Maurice “Rocket” Richard Trophy and fifth Art Ross Trophy, posting the highest goal total by any player since 2007-08 and most points since 1995-96.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Kirill Kaprizov
summary.description:
Kirill "The Thrill" Kaprizov is an exciting player who can create scoring chances in a variety of ways.  Here he shows why he is such a presence anywhere on the ice, emerging from the corner after winning a puck battle before shooting from deep behind the goal line and banking the puck off the goaltender’s mask for the goal. Kaprizov emerged onto the scene in 2020-21 and led the Wild in both goals and points in each of his first three NHL campaigns, setting single-season franchise records in each category along the way.

summary.name: Jack Hughes
summary.description:
On the power play, Jack Hughes picks up the puck near his blueline before turning to wheel up-ice.  Gaining speed, he breaks through Ottawa's defense by protecting the puck on his backhand before bringing it to his forehand and tucking it in five-hole. In his fourth NHL season, at age 21, Hughes collected 43 goals and 99 points in 2022-23 to post the highest goal total by a Devils player since 2008-09 and set a franchise record for points in one season.

summary.name: Sidney Crosby
summary.description:
Voted the “Most Complete Player” by his peers in the NHLPA poll for the fourth consecutive season in 2022-23, Pittsburgh Penguins captain Sidney Crosby continues to excel after 18 seasons in the NHL.  On the road in Colorado, Crosby gets a pass in the middle of the ice from teammate Jake Guentzel before streaking into the offensive zone where he snipes his signature backhand shot top shelf to give Pittsburgh a 1-0 lead in the second period.

summary.name: Erik Karlsson
summary.description:
In what has been a resurgence year for three-time James Norris Memorial Trophy winner Erik Karlsson, he makes a great individual effort on this play to earn a beautiful assist. Having his best season wearing a San Jose Sharks uniform, the smooth-skating Karlsson begins the play off the faceoff with a quick move at the blueline to evade the defender. He then skates the puck down near the corner before looping back up to the point. Not only does he create more space for himself but now all eyes are on Karlsson, which creates a wide-open Steven Lorentz who Karlsson finds for the goal. It has been a remarkable year statistically for Karlsson having bested all of his previous seasons in points.

summary.name: Clayton Keller
summary.description:
Clayton Keller roofs a backhand top shelf on the breakaway to score his second of three goals in the game for his first career hat trick. Keller set career highs in goals (37), assists (49) and points (86) in 2022-23, the second straight season in which he led the Arizona Coyotes in both goals and points. His 86 points in 2022-23 equaled the most by a Coyotes player in one season, matching Keith Tkachuk’s totals from 1996-97 – the team’s first season in Arizona after moving from Winnipeg.

summary.description:
Jacob Markstrom goes old-school with a two-pad stack to rob Mark Scheifele of a sure goal with a worldly glove save. The Calgary Flames goaltender, who was a finalist for the Vezina Trophy in 2021-22, went on to lead his club to a 3-2 win over the Winnipeg Jets.

summary.name: Jonathan Toews
summary.description:
In perhaps his final game wearing a Chicago Blackhawks uniform, captain Jonathan Toews scores a goal in the team’s 2022-23 finale, at home against the Philadelphia Flyers – the team Chicago beat when Toews hoisted the Stanley Cup for the first time in 2010. Toews begins the play by winning an offensive zone faceoff, then heads to the slot where he redirects a shot-pass into the net for Chicago’s third goal of the game. The three-time Stanley Cup champion and Conn Smythe Trophy winner receives a roaring cheer from the home crowd.

summary.description:
Slick and shifty Johnny Gaudreau goes for a skate, controlling the puck while the Columbus Blue Jackets are changing. “Johnny Hockey” then breaks up the ice, skates behind the net and tucks it home for a gorgeous individual effort play. His tying goal in the third period helped the club rally for an eventual overtime win – their first victory of the 2022-23 season.

summary.name: Tim Stützle
summary.description:
Off the faceoff near the end of an Ottawa power play, Brady Tkachuk retrieves the puck off the boards to get it back to Tim Stützle. With Sidney Crosby pursuing, Stützle evades him with a nice drag to the middle of the ice and quick burst of acceleration before firing home a wrister for his 20th goal of the season. The German-born winger set career highs in goals (39) and points (90) in 2022-23, his third NHL season.

summary.description:
Seattle Kraken forward Jordan Eberle fools everyone with a beautiful backhand goal to excite the home crowd in Seattle. After receiving the cross-ice feed from defenseman Adam Larsson, Eberle instantly twists it around to his backhand and roofs it to beat Winnipeg Jets goaltender David Rittich.

Vancouver Canucks defenseman Quinn Hughes, a gifted skater with excellent offensive abilities, does almost a full lap in the offensive zone around San Jose Sharks players before sniping the puck top shelf for his first goal of the 2022-23 season.

summary.description:
Anaheim Ducks forward Trevor Zegras streaks through the middle lane with speed where he receives a sauce pass from teammate Ryan Strome. Quickly running out of real estate and instead of staying on the backhand for a poor angle shot, Zegras goes through his legs to go top shelf on the far side, once again showing why he is an exciting player to watch and one of the most creative players in the NHL.

summary.description:
Sebastian Aho, a well-rounded forward who contributes in all areas of the rink, opens the scoring with a shorthanded goal for the Carolina Hurricanes. The puck gets turned over at the Carolina blueline, where Aho picks it up and rushes up ice with speed. On the breakaway, he makes a move to freeze the goaltender before tucking it five-hole on the backhand.

summary.name: Jack Eichel
summary.description:
In his first full season with the Vegas Golden Knights, Jack Eichel skates the puck around the offensive zone for nearly 15 seconds before netting the game winner in overtime. As he makes his move toward the net, Eichel brings the puck to his forehand at the last second before tucking it home to bring the Vegas crowd to its feet.

summary.name: Brayden Point
summary.description:
Brayden Point has been electric in establishing himself as an elite player in the NHL. Here he wheels up the ice and dances through three Seattle Kraken defenders before roofing a backhand beauty. Point has consistently been a key offensive player for the Tampa Bay Lightning, leading the playoffs in goals during the team’s Stanley Cup-winning runs in both 2020 and 2021. In 2022-23, Point scored 51 goals to become the third different player in Lightning history with a 50-goal season.

summary.name: Mitch Marner
summary.description:
During three-on-three play in overtime, Mitch Marner regroups in his own zone for a drop pass before heading up the ice with speed. After gaining the offensive zone, Marner slows before using a quick burst to get around his check to the net where he leaps over the sprawling goaltender to tuck home a beautiful game-winner. Marner set career highs in assists (69) and points (99) in 2022-23, with his assist count standing as the highest by a Toronto Maple Leafs player since 1993-94 when Doug Gilmour had 84.

summary.name: Elias Pettersson
summary.description:
What a night for Vancouver Canucks forward Elias Pettersson who secures his fifth point of the game when he one-times the game-tying goal with just 80 seconds remaining in the third period. If that wasn’t enough, he then scores the deciding goal in the shootout to earn Vancouver a 6-5 victory against the Seattle Kraken. Playing in his fifth NHL season, Pettersson collected 39-63—102 in 80 games in 2022-23 to set career highs in goals, assists and points and become Vancouver’s first 100-point player in a dozen years.

summary.name: Opening Ice
summary.description: Get ready to witness the NHL’s rising stars like never before with Opening Ice. This set features 20 heart-pounding highlights from players who have notched their first career goal in the 2021-22 and 2022-23 seasons.

summary.name: Connor McDavid
summary.description:
Connor McDavid set career highs in goals, assists and points in 2022-23 while also becoming the fourth player in NHL history to register more than 152 points in a single season – and first since Mario Lemieux in 1995-96. This highlight begins with a brilliant McDavid assist versus the Ottawa Senators on Feb. 11, 2023, as McDavid steals the puck from Thomas Chabot and spins to protect it before finding Ryan McLeod for a shorthanded goal on the road. In the following play, McDavid nets his 60th goal of the season on March 22, 2023, versus the Arizona Coyotes. In overtime, McDavid streaks up the middle of the ice where he receives a beautiful backhand pass from Leon Draisaitl. On the breakaway, McDavid hits the post and the puck squirts out to the boards where Draisaitl wins the battle and feeds McDavid again – who this time buries for the milestone goal and game-winner at home.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Patrice Bergeron
summary.description:
Boston Bruins captain Patrice Bergeron leads the rush up the ice before dishing the puck to Brad Marchand and driving the net to create space for Marchand to eventually score the goal that would earn Bergeron his 1,000th career NHL point. Marchand immediately recognizes the accomplishment and teammates flood the ice to celebrate. At the time, Bergeron became the 94th player in history to record 1,000 points. Known for his two-way abilities, Bergeron extended his record by winning his sixth Frank J. Selke Trophy in 2022-23.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Alex Ovechkin
summary.description:
Becoming just the third player in history to score 800 goals, Alex Ovechkin hits the mark in style by completing a hat trick for the milestone tally. The play begins with a forecheck by Anthony Mantha that causes a turnover. Mantha throws the puck out in front where the pass gets deflected and bounces into Evgeny Kuznetsov’s shin pad. With the puck bouncing around in front of the net, Mantha corrals it enough to get it over to Ovechkin who buries the milestone goal. On the road in Chicago, hats are thrown onto the ice from the stands as Washington Capitals teammates flood the ice to celebrate the achievement. Just 10 days later, Ovechkin would score goal #802 to surpass Gordie Howe (801) for second place all-time behind Wayne Gretzky (894).

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Erik Karlsson
summary.description:
With his 25th goal of the season and second of the game, San Jose Sharks defenseman Erik Karlsson reached 100 points in a season for the first time in his career. At age 32, Karlsson becomes the first defenseman to record 100+ points in a season at age 30 or older. Overall, he is the sixth different defenseman in NHL history to hit the mark at any age, following Bobby Orr (6x), Paul Coffey (5x), Brian Leetch, Al MacInnis and Denis Potvin. On the milestone play, Karlsson receives a pass from teammate Tomas Hertl, changes the angle of his shot to use the goaltender screen to his advantage and shoots the puck through traffic into the net.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Linus Ullmark
summary.description:
Linus Ullmark becomes the eighth goaltender in NHL history to shoot the puck into the net for a goal (Ron Hextall did it twice) and the first Boston Bruins goalie to do so. It was the 16th time in League history that a goaltender was credited with a goal in the regular season or playoffs, including instances when goalies were designated because they were the last player to touch the puck before an opponent scored on their own net. With just under a minute to go in Vancouver and the Bruins holding a 2-1 lead, Ullmark launches the puck over everyone and into the net. The excitement of both him and his teammates is unforgettable during a career-year for Ullmark, who tied a franchise record with 40 wins alongside a .938 save percentage and 1.89 goals-against average.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Steven Stamkos
summary.description:
Tampa Bay Lightning captain Steven Stamkos becomes the 47th player in NHL history to join the 500-goal club. During the first period in Vancouver, the two-time Maurice “Rocket” Richard Trophy winner goes to the net while teammate Alex Killorn makes a nice move to get around a defender before feeding Stamkos for the tap-in goal. Teammates flood the ice to congratulate Stamkos, who ends up netting three goals for the hatty in a 5-2 win.
